newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open lower, profit-taking cited.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open lower, profit-taking cited.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened lower on Friday as the market was caught in a mild bout of profit-taking, analysts said.

Near the start of a session that will include the release of one consumer sentiment indicator but no official government economic reports, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 4/32 to 97-19/32, yielding 6.56 percent.
At the shorter end of the maturity range, two-year notes were down 1/32 to 99-31/32, yielding 5.89 percent.
Three- and six-month bill rates were each down one basis point to 5.18 percent and 5.19 percent, respectively.
Five-year notes were down 2/32 to 99-16/32, yielding 6.12 percent and 10-year notes were dwon 2/32 to 98-31/32, yielding 6.27 percent.

"There's some profit-taking occurring but not much is going on today," said Kim Rupert, senior economist at Standard & Poor's MMS. "It should be a pretty lethargic day. We've seen a lot of volatility in the last week and I think the market's pretty tired."
Rupert said the market faces resistance at 113-27 on the September T-bond contract. She cited support for the September bond at Tuesday's high of 113-10 and then at 113-07, "a congestion area."
Overnight profit-taking included some selling of 10-year notes, she added.

"We were pretty much unchanged," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds. "Then New York came in and took some profits. The dollar is off its highs. But nothing major is really going on. Activity is on the light side."

William Hornbarger, fixed-income strategist at A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc, said there was talk of Asian central bank selling of two- and three-year notes, sales rumored to be related to potential currency intervention.
Hornbarger also pointed to profit-taking.
"There's a little bit of profit-taking," he said. "And we're still seeing some of the auction distribution from the Treasury refunding last week."
The $38.0 billion in three-, 10- and 30-year securities that the Treasury sold last week in a three-part auction all settle on August 15.
That settlement was putting upward pressure on the Federal funds rate, analysts said.
Federal funds were trading at 5-3/4 percent in early activity, above the Fed's 5-1/2 percent target for the rate.
"As a result, the (Fed's open market) desk should be in (adding temporary reserves to the banking system) with repos," said MMS.
Some market participants will also be distracted by the PGA golf tournament taking place in New York, analysts said.
"Everyone will be watching the P.G.A. (golf championship) at Winged Foot (in New York) today," said Rupert.

"The scene in New York is complicated by the local golf tournament, which is drawing scads of people who sell securities out to (Mamaroneck), along with a lot of their customers," said Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics.
The opening round of the 79th P.G.A. Championship was played on Thursday.
